title: Research Fellow: AI-moderated Interviews at Scale: The Trust in Healthcare Study
description:
Surgo Health is requesting proposals for research projects building on our dataset focused on the healthcare trust landscape. While declining public trust in the U.S. healthcare system is widely documented through conventional survey methods, the underlying, individual-level drivers of this erosion often remain unclear.

To address this gap, our dataset explores trust dynamics across medical providers, health institutions, social media, and artificial intelligence, while highlighting actionable pathways for restoring confidence. The data encompasses both a detailed questionnaire battery and in-depth qualitative dialogues gathered by Derin®, our AI-moderated interviewing system.

Designed as a randomized, counterbalanced study, the dataset enables direct methodological comparisons between standard survey approaches and AI-moderated conversational interviews. It spans roughly 2,000 respondents across two distinct research panels. It has 6,000 completed interviews alongside extensive survey batteries, standard demographic indicators, and population weighting factors.

We are seeking research proposals that:

•
Advance the narrative on trust & healthcare -contribute to contemporary thinking on this subject in the U.S.

•
Leverage the conversations - projects should examine the reasoning, experiences, or context revealed when respondents elaborate, going beyond what closed items already capture.

•
Use the dataset - research questions should be answerable with the current dataset and not require funding for new data collection

•
Publishable - proposals should aim for peer-reviewed publication, with rigorous methodology.

We encourage proposals that move beyond showing that conversational interviews produce more detail, focusing instead on for whom, under what conditions, and through what mechanisms conversational data adds value. Projects will be given access to the full dataset and documentation, and can integrate external data (such as ACS, provider density, or state health policy indicators) via the harmonized geographic and demographic variables in the dataset.

Research Focus Areas

We welcome proposals in areas below, but also encourage you to submit proposals that are adjacent to these areas.

•
Trust in healthcare - drivers of trust erosion and recovery; public perspectives on AI in healthcare; decisions made against medical advice; institutional versus individual trust; and perceptions of the pharmaceutical industry.

•
Survey methodology - variations in response quality by education, age, income, geography, and political views; order and carry-over effects across modes; effort signatures; construct validity of trust items; and turn-level drop-off in conversational surveys.

•
Interviewer design and conversation dynamics - probing strategies and sequencing; respondent responses (elaboration vs. new disclosures); interviewer neutrality; and managing sensitive disclosures.

•
Computational methods - analysis pipelines for transcript data, including predicting closed-ended responses from conversational text (and vice versa).

Proposals should be 1-2 pages and outline:

•
Core contribution - how the research builds beyond existing literature

•
Use of qualitative data - what insights the conversational responses provide beyond standard closed-ended items.

•
Practical application - key decisions or practice changes informed by the findings.

•
Analytical plan - key variables, panel-specific estimates, and analytical approaches for randomized and observational factors.

•
Publication goals - target journals and expected outputs.

Program Structure

•
Surgo Health will select two to three proposals based on:

• Practical relevance and research depth

• Feasibility with available data

• Alignment with Surgo Health research priorities

• Potential for publication in high-impact journals

Selected projects will receive:

•
Stipend amount: $6,000 in compensation upon successful submission of draft to Surgo

• Weekly touch-point me

title: Technical Project Manager
description:
About the role

Sporty is looking for an experienced IT/IS Project Manager to coordinate and drive Information Technology (IT) and Information Security (IS) initiatives across our global organisation.

The role works across IT, Information Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Platform/DevOps, and business teams to ensure projects and operational initiatives have clear ownership, priorities, timelines, and measurable outcomes.

A significant part of the role focuses on Information Security delivery, including vulnerability remediation, Red Team and Blue Team activities, and security improvement initiatives.

Work is distributed across multiple teams and Jira environments. You will be responsible for maintaining consolidated visibility, identifying delivery risks and trends, and ensuring important work is driven through to completion.

This is a hands-on delivery role. We are looking for someone who takes ownership, creates structure, proactively identifies problems, and drives actions rather than simply tracking and reporting status.

 

What you'll be doing

IT Project & Initiative Management

• Lead internal IT initiatives from requirements and planning through implementation, rollout, and operational handover.

• Define scope, milestones, ownership, dependencies, and success criteria.

• Coordinate delivery across IT, Engineering, Infrastructure, Security, and business teams.

• Proactively manage risks, blockers, priorities, and cross-team dependencies.

• Drive decisions and ensure projects progress through to completion.

Projects may cover areas such as IAM/SSO, Google Workspace, Slack, GitHub, enterprise SaaS, endpoint technology, AWS/cloud services, corporate connectivity, internal systems, and IT automation.

Information Security Delivery Management

• Coordinate security-related initiatives and tasks across Information Security, Engineering, Infrastructure, Platform, Red Team, and Blue Team.

• Track vulnerability findings and remediation activities through to validation and closure.

• Coordinate follow-up actions from penetration testing, Red Team/Blue Team activities, security reviews, incidents, and security improvement programmes.

• Ensure security tasks have appropriate priority, ownership, target dates, and remediation plans.

• Identify stalled or high-risk items and drive follow-up, prioritisation, and escalation where necessary.

The role does not perform security testing or vulnerability analysis directly, but should understand security concepts sufficiently to manage the delivery process effectively.

Jira, Task Governance & Analytics

• Maintain visibility of IT/IS work distributed across multiple Jira systems, projects, teams, and workflows.

• Establish consolidated reporting across different Jira environments and maintain appropriate data quality and traceability.

• Monitor backlog, aging, remediation progress, overdue work, throughput, and other relevant delivery metrics.

• Analyse historical and current data to identify trends, bottlenecks, recurring issues, and deteriorating performance.

• Automate data collection, aggregation, and reporting where practical.

The objective is not simply to maintain dashboards, but to turn fragmented task data into actionable management information.

Cross-Team Coordination & Governance

• Act as a coordination point across Information Security, IT, Engineering, Infrastructure, Platform/DevOps, system owners, business functions, and management.

• Maintain clear visibility of risks, issues, dependencies, decisions, and commitments.

• Resolve unclear ownership and facilitate prioritisation where teams have competing priorities.

• Provide concise management reporting focused on progress, trends, risks, exceptions, and decisions required.

• Establish appropriate project and task governance without introducing unnecessary process.

 

 

 

What you'll bring

• 5+ years of experience in IT/IS Project Management, Security Project

title: Product Manager
description:
Toast creates technology to help restaurants and local businesses succeed in a digital world, helping business owners operate, increase sales, engage customers, and keep employees happy.

We're looking for a Product Manager for Fraud & Risk who wants to understand how fraud really happens and to build products that stop it at scale. You're comfortable with ambiguity and you like hard trade-offs, like loss vs. friction or automation vs. human review. Your decisions rest on data, customer insight and strong cross-functional partnerships. And last, but not least, you know that a team succeeds because of its people, and you want to help build an environment where we can all do our best work.

This is a chance to shape the risk platform behind one of the largest restaurant payments businesses in the US. You'll use machine learning and AI to protect restaurants and help Toast grow. 

Who We Are

The Fraud & Risk team keeps Toast, our restaurants and their guests safe from fraud and financial loss. We also make it fast and easy for restaurants to get onboarded and get paid. The team owns:

• Merchant onboarding and underwriting (KYC/KYB)

• Transaction and payout risk monitoring

• The fraud rules and decisioning platform

• Settlement reserves

• Chargebacks and disputes

Our job is to balance loss prevention against growth. We stop bad actors without adding friction for the great majority of restaurants that are doing the right thing. We work closely with Risk Operations, Payments, Compliance and Legal. We operate like a small startup with high ambitions and a focus on speed, experimentation and iteration.

A day in the life (Responsibilities) 

• Drive and prioritize the roadmap for your area of Fraud & Risk. Balance fraud loss reduction, merchant experience and business growth.

• Set the strategy for detecting and preventing fraud across the merchant lifecycle: onboarding, payments, payouts and disputes.

• Partner with data science and engineering to improve risk models, rules and decisioning. Define the right trade-offs between catching fraud and avoiding false positives.

• Build AI-driven automation that scales our risk and chargeback operations, such as agent-assisted reviews and automated dispute responses.

• Understand the needs of restaurants, their guests and our internal Risk Operations analysts. Use customer conversations, investigations, data analysis, ops feedback and industry intelligence.

• Define and own success metrics such as fraud loss rates, chargeback rates and win rates, auto-approval rates and operational efficiency.

• Work with Compliance, Legal, Payments and external partners such as processors, card networks and risk vendors to deliver solutions that are compliant and scalable.

• Write clear product requirements and work closely with designers and engineers to bring them to life.

• Be a great teammate, always.

What you'll need to thrive (Requirements)

• 3+ years of product management experience, ideally in fraud, risk, payments, fintech, or trust & safety

• A working knowledge of the payments ecosystem: card networks, processors and acquirers, chargebacks and disputes, and KYC/KYB

• Strong analytical skills. You're comfortable digging into data yourself, with SQL as a strong plus, and you understand how ML models and rules engines make decisions.

• Sound judgment in weighing risk against customer friction, and the ability to make good calls with incomplete information, including during live fraud incidents

• Proven ownership of a product that supports company strategy and meets defined business objectives

• A track record of working well with cross-functional partners, especially operations, compliance and legal teams

• The ability to thrive and self-prioritize across multiple projects in a fast-paced environment with tight deadlines

• Active use of AI tools and best practices in your own work to drive efficiency

• Exceptional attention to detail

title: Associate Attorney

We have significant expertise in balance sheet and securitized lending, and CMBS and agency origination and servicing, with experience in virtually every aspect of real estate finance transactions.

Reiferson Dee is seeking to add an Associate Attorney to the team. In this role, you will represent lenders in sophisticated commercial real estate finance transactions, with a primary focus on multifamily housing originations, structured finance transactions, and securitization due diligence. You will work closely with clients, attorneys, lenders, and other transaction participants to structure, negotiate, document, and close complex commercial real estate financing transactions.

The Associate Attorney will independently manage multiple transactions while benefiting from robust training and professional development with the firm’s Managing Member and other experienced members of the firm. This includes hands-on mentorship and shadowing opportunities designed to deepen your knowledge of the firm’s practice and provide exposure to sophisticated commercial real estate finance transactions. The role also offers a path toward membership. We are seeking an attorney with strong commercial real estate finance experience, exceptional legal drafting and negotiation skills, attention to detail, and a desire to continue learning and growing within an experienced team.

Note: This is a remote position and requires an initial three-week, in-person training period at the firm’s Canonsburg, Pennsylvania office.

Essential Responsibilities:

•
Multifamily Loan Originations: Represent lenders in the origination, structuring, negotiation, and documentation of multifamily commercial real estate loans, including conventional, affordable housing, manufactured housing, seniors housing, and student housing transactions.

•
Securitization Due Diligence: Conduct comprehensive mortgage loan due diligence and prepare exceptions to representations and warranties made to investors in connection with securitized loan pools.

•
Structured Finance Transactions: Represent clients in the origination, structuring, negotiation, and documentation of structured finance vehicles, including lines of credit, long-term financing facilities, participation interests, and PC swap transactions.

•
Transaction Management: Manage multiple commercial real estate finance transactions simultaneously, ensuring deadlines, client expectations, and closing timelines are consistently met.

•
Legal Drafting & Negotiation: Draft, review, and negotiate loan documents, transaction agreements, legal opinions, and related financing documentation while identifying and mitigating legal risk.

•
Client & Stakeholder Collaboration: Communicate regularly with clients, opposing counsel, lenders, title companies, servicers, and other transaction participants to facilitate efficient transaction execution and maintain exceptional client service.

•
Legal Research & Risk Analysis: Analyze legal issues affecting commercial real estate finance transactions and provide practical, business-oriented legal advice to clients and firm attorneys.

•
Training & Professional Development: Participate in ongoing training, mentorship, and shadowing opportunities with the Managing Member and other experienced attorneys to deepen knowledge of the firm’s practice and further develop expertise in complex commercial real estate finance transactions.

title: Community Engagement Manager, Data Centers (New York)
description:
About Anthropic

Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

About the role

Anthropic is building AI systems that will shape the trajectory of one of the most consequential technologies in human history. That work requires physical infrastructure at significant scale, and building that infrastructure the right way means being a real, long-term partner to the communities where we operate.

We are looking for a Community Engagement Manager in New York to join our Public Policy team and serve as Anthropic's on-the-ground presence in the communities where our data centers are sited, built, and operated. This is not a communications role or a government affairs role, though you will do elements of both. It is a relationship role: your job is to make Anthropic a trusted, visible, and valued neighbor, from the earliest stages of site selection through construction and long-term operations.

You will be the connective tissue between Anthropic's Policy and Infrastructure teams and the local officials, community organizations, economic development partners, and residents who have a stake in what we build. You will surface concerns before they escalate, translate our technical and operational plans into clear local benefits, and build the coalitions that allow us to move quickly and responsibly. Because Anthropic's infrastructure footprint is still early in its growth, you will also help write the playbook: the processes you build in your first markets are the ones we will use as we expand.

You will travel regularly across New York State, including upstate communities, up to 50% of the time, and occasionally to other Anthropic data center markets.

Key responsibilities

•
Build and maintain trusted, sustained relationships with town, village, city, and county elected officials and administrators, planning and zoning boards, local industrial development agencies, state agencies, economic development organizations, community groups, civic leaders, labor and building trades organizations, educational institutions, and workforce partners in the New York data center markets you cover

•
Develop and execute a community engagement strategy for each of your markets, spanning site selection, pre-development, construction, and ongoing operations

•
Build external coalitions, host education and listening sessions, and design local solutions that deliver real benefits to the communities where we operate

•
Represent Anthropic in public forums, town halls, planning hearings, community events, and local media

•
Monitor community sentiment and local political dynamics, and advise internal teams on risks, opportunities, and the right pace and posture for engagement

•
Partner with the Real Estate and Infrastructure team to bring community input into how projects are planned, communicated, and delivered, not just how they are announced, including public comment and environmental review processes

•
Work with the Communications team to develop proactive, locally relevant messaging

•
Coordinate charitable giving, community investment, and economic development commitments in your markets, including managing nonprofit partner relationships

•
Partner with the Energy and Sustainability team to explain our approach to environmental stewardship and respond to questions about power, water, and land use, including how New York's energy and climate policies and grid conditions shape our plans

•
Build a community engagement playbook and repeatable processes that scale as Anthropic's infrastructure footprint grows

Minimum qualifications

•
Experience in community affairs, public affairs, economic development, government relations, local or state government, or a closely related field

title: Associate Systems Engineer

Job Summary
We are seeking a dedicated and detail-oriented Associate Systems Support Engineer to join our IT operations team. The successful candidate will be responsible for monitoring and maintaining the performance of critical systems, ensuring the uptime and availability of applications and infrastructure. • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, or a related field, or equivalent work experience.

• Basic knowledge of SQL databases, including monitoring and troubleshooting techniques.

• Understanding of Windows Server administration and IIS management.

• Experience with monitoring server uptime, performance metrics, and alert management.

• Proficient in troubleshooting system issues and performing root cause analysis.

• Strong analytical skills and attention to detail to ensure high-quality service delivery.

• Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal, with the ability to work collaboratively in a team environment.

• Understanding of monitoring tools like AppDynamics and LogicMonitor.

• Knowledge of ITIL best practices and frameworks.

• Excellente connaissance des normes réglementaires et professionnelles applicables aux médecins du Nouveau-Brunswick.

title: RevOps Architect
description:
As a Growth Operations Architect, you will play a critical role in the experience and success of every client you manage. You will be responsible for working with a small group of clients (3-5) to develop a growth operations roadmap, design solutions to business problems, and manage the execution of the solutions you design.
This is a strategic role that involves guiding business conversations with stakeholders - usually sales and marketing leadership. This is not a systems administrator role, though past experience as a CRM admin is a plus. Successful architects help clients understand what they should do - they don’t wait for clients to assign work.
What You’ll Do

• Manage onboarding and facilitate workshops - Guide new clients through a structured onboarding process to ensure alignment. Partner with consultants to understand each client’s Go-To-Market (GTM) strategy, processes, and systems.

• Build and execute operational roadmaps - Maintain prioritized roadmap documentation for each client, ensuring projects align with business goals.

• Manage project execution - Drive the end-to-end project lifecycle, from discovery and planning to implementation and post-deployment monitoring.

• Own client success - Act as the main liaison between clients and internal resources, ensuring all projects and tasks run smoothly.

• Run sprint meetings and client reviews - Conduct regular sprint check-ins, deliver ongoing status updates to clients, and lead monthly and quarterly reviews.

• Triage and manage client requests - Quickly assess, prioritize and assign ad hoc client needs.

What You Won’t Do

• Lots of admin work - While you may spend some time in clients' systems, you will work closely with our admin team to design things that they build.

• Take support tickets - Operations support is something we offer, but an architect is not responsible for providing support in most cases.

• Sales or marketing - we don’t do outsourced sales or marketing, so while our architects are expected to have a deep understanding of what our clients do, it is not their job to know how clients should sell or market.

Must-Haves

• 5+ years of experience in Sales Ops, Marketing Ops, RevOps, or GTM Ops

• Strong knowledge of Salesforce or HubSpot, either as an administrator or through managing CRM implementations or updates

• Proven ability to manage strategy and projects in Revenue Operations environments

• Strong organizational skills with the ability to prioritize and oversee multiple initiatives

• High attention to detail

• Excellent written and verbal communication skills

• A growth mindset with the ability to quickly learn and adapt

Nice-to-Haves

• Experience in SaaS startups

• Background in professional services or consulting

• Experience on a sales and/or marketing team

• Familiarity with project management frameworks (e.g., Agile methodologies, sprint planning)

All your information will be kept confidential according to EEO guidelines.
Iceberg offers competitive benefits, including unlimited time off, medical insurance, 401(k) with match, and more.
Iceberg is the sales and marketing operations team for growing companies. We specialize in architecting and building unified systems. We partner primarily with B2B, high-growth, VC- and PE-backed companies. We implement strong sales and marketing systems by providing services across sales ops, marketing ops, revenue strategy, data analysis, and more. Our team is small but expanding quickly and we are looking for the right people to help us get to the next level.

title: Capital Planning & Stress Testing Program Manager
description:

Capital Planning & Stress Testing Program Manager Location
Nationwide, MI 48098 Job Summary
The Capital Planning & Stress Testing Program Manager leads Flagstar’s stress testing and capital planning processes, reporting to the Director of Capital Planning & Stress Testing. This role coordinates cross-functional teams to execute stress test plans, ensure regulatory compliance, and align with capital management policies. Responsibilities include developing and integrating stress testing processes, overseeing documentation, guiding scenario design, and preparing reports for senior management and regulators. The manager ensures that capital planning is effective, meets governance standards, and supports strategic decisions. This role exists to ensure the bank’s capital planning exercises are executed efficiently, meet regulatory expectations, and support sound strategic decision-making. Job Responsibilities:
JOB RESPONSIBILITIES

• Program Leadership & Plan Coordination: Leads the bank’s stress testing program, coordinating input from multiple departments to collect and integrate all necessary data and materials. Maintains and updates key capital planning documents (e.g., capital plan narrative, policies, contingency plans) to ensure the stress testing process is cohesive and aligned with business objectives.

• Scenario Design & Challenge Oversight: Leads internal stress test scenarios informed by the bank’s idiosyncratic risks (Risk ID inventory) and evaluates capital adequacy under adverse conditions. • Quality Assurance & Compliance: Ensures the consistency and reliability of stress test results through strong quality controls and data governance. Supports and addresses any findings from regulatory, risk, or internal audits and ensures continuous compliance with all relevant policies and regulatory requirements throughout the stress testing cycle.

• Proactively manage examination requests, company resources, program risks, and required deliverables, as well as the day-to-day planning and resource allocation.

• Responsible for talent management functions including: employment, performance evaluations, staff development/training, disciplinary actions, succession planning and ensuring all staff comply with compliance requirements.

ADDITIONAL ACCOUNTABILITIES

• Strategic Alignment: Works under the direction of the CPST Director to ensure that stress testing activities support the bank’s strategic goals for capital adequacy and risk management. • Governance and Policy Adherence: Upholds the governance framework for capital planning. Ensures that all activities follow the approved Capital Planning & Stress Testing policies and the governance standards set by management committees (CMC, ERMC) and the Board. All documentation and processes should withstand regulatory scrutiny and internal audit standards.

• Experience running LLMs underreal costand latency budgets in production.

We are seeking a hands-on Cybersecurity Engineer to deploy, manage, and optimise Privileged Access Management (PAM), Data Loss Prevention (DLP), and Email Security solutions. Senior Clinical Research Associate
Valencia, California - REMOTE FOR THE RIGHT CANDIDATE | WEST COAST BASED PREFERRED
Join Advanced Bionics as a Senior Clinical Research Associate and take a lead role in the operational execution of global medical device clinical studies from study start-up through close-out. You will manage complex investigative sites, drive study quality and performance, identify and mitigate operational risks, and serve as an experienced clinical operations resource to study teams while helping advance innovative hearing healthcare technologies.
Responsibilities

• Independently lead the operational execution of assigned global clinical studies from site start-up through close-out in accordance with study protocols, ICH-GCP, ISO 14155, FDA regulations, and applicable international regulatory requirements.

• Conduct site qualification, initiation, interim monitoring, and close-out visits (SQV, SIV, IMV, and COV) for complex or high-priority studies.

• Lead site activation, investigator training, study device accountability, close-out planning, and other activities required to achieve study milestones.

• Serve as the primary operational lead for assigned investigative sites, monitoring enrollment, site performance, protocol compliance, and data quality while proactively identifying and mitigating risks.

• Independently resolve complex monitoring findings, protocol deviations, data queries, and site-performance issues while escalating significant risks with recommended solutions.

• Maintain inspection-ready TMF/eTMF and investigator site documentation, support audits and regulatory inspections, and promote consistent application of clinical quality standards.

• Partner with Clinical Trial Management, Data Management, Biostatistics, Regulatory Affairs, Quality, Medical Affairs, and external vendors while mentoring CRAs and supporting clinical operations process improvements.

More about you

• Bachelor's degree in Life Sciences, Nursing, Biomedical Engineering, or another related scientific discipline.

• Minimum 5 years of clinical research experience, including at least 2 years of independent site monitoring.

• Experience managing multiple clinical sites and working with CTMS, EDC, and eTMF systems.

• Strong knowledge of ICH-GCP, ISO 14155, FDA regulations, clinical monitoring, site management, and data quality.

• Demonstrated ability to independently manage complex studies, multiple priorities, operational risks, and site-performance challenges.

• Strong organizational, communication, problem-solving, and time-management skills.

• Ability to travel approximately 30-50% to study sites, conferences, and other study-related activities.

Preferred qualifications include: a Master's degree or equivalent; ACRP-CRA, ACRP-CP, or SOCRA CCRP certification; experience in Class III medical device clinical trials, global multicenter studies, FDA IDE/PMA or EU MDR clinical studies; experience mentoring junior CRAs or leading monitoring activities; and knowledge of Risk-Based Monitoring/RbQM.

title: Senior Data Analyst
description:
ROLE PURPOSE
As Senior Data Analyst, you turn iiDENTIFii ’s data into decisions the business can act on with confidence. Business questions rarely arrive fully formed, so your craft is to shape a broadly worded question into something that can genuinely be answered, answer it well, and land that answer with the people who need to act on it.
This is a senior, hands-on analysis role that sits close to both the business and the data platform. You are comfortable interrogating a messy dataset in the morning and presenting a customer engagement analysis to leadership in the afternoon. You bring analytical depth, sound judgement on data quality and governance, and the communication skill to translate complex findings into decisions non-technical stakeholders can act on.
You work the lifecycle end to end: framing the question, modelling and interrogating the data, drawing out the insight, and seeing the recommendation through to a decision and its adoption. We care more about how well you think, how clearly you communicate and how curious you are about how data is built than about the particular tools you have used before. Strong analysts come from many backgrounds and industries, and we would like to hear from all of them.
What Good Looks Like in the First Six Months

• You own the core business and client reporting, and the definitions behind those numbers are documented, consistent and trusted across teams

• Recurring reporting that is rebuilt by hand today runs to a schedule, with quality checks attached

• At least one piece of analysis you initiated, rather than were asked for, has changed a product, operational or commercial decision

• Product, engineering and commercial treat you as the person to ask about what the data actually says

ROLE TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
Reporting, Dashboards & Self-Service

• Own end-to-end reporting for the key business metrics, keeping definitions consistent and trusted across teams

• Build and maintain dashboards and self-service tools that let teams find and act on insight without going through you

• Own recurring client reporting end to end: definition, automation, quality assurance, delivery and the follow-up conversation - credible explaining a number, or a discrepancy, directly to a client’s team

• Handle ad-hoc requests with good judgement: establish the real question, deliver a clear and actionable answer, and prioritise sensibly when several arrive at once

• Choose the tool that fits the purpose across our broad set of reporting and visualisation technologies, matching the right one to the audience, the question and the shelf life of the answer

Product & User Behaviour Analysis

• Analyse user behaviour across our products to identify trends, friction points and opportunities, and turn findings into concrete recommendations

• Track and report on engagement, retention and customer journey metrics, flagging risks and opportunities proactively rather than on request

• Apply appropriate statistical rigour, including cohort analysis, significance testing, forecasting and seasonality, so that recommendations hold up when they are challenged

• Design and evaluate experiments with product, and be clear about what a result does and does not prove

• Investigate anomalies and unexpected patterns, and work out whether what you are seeing is genuine signal, a data quality issue, or noise

Automation & Data Foundations

• Automate recurring analysis and reporting so that regular outputs run reliably to a schedule with quality checks, rather than being rebuilt by hand each cycle

• Build and maintain your own analytical models and reusable assets on top of the curated data, so knowledge compounds instead of living in one-off queries

• Specify what the analytics layer needs from upstream data (the sources, structures, definitions and refresh frequencies) and work with the engineering team to get there

• Understand the data platform well enough to be a genuine partner to engineering: where

Orbis is a technology company that delivers sovereign intelligence and decision capabilities to the United States Government and its allies. We convert complex information and operational systems into decisive outcomes, giving public institutions and critical enterprises the tools to move faster, see clearer, and act first in an increasingly contested world.

We are not a consulting firm and not a systems integrator. Every Orbis team is built around practitioners who have operated at the mission edge, and every engagement is judged on one thing: whether it produces working capability, not slide decks. title: Head of Capital
description:
Relay is fundamentally reshaping how goods move in an online era. Backed by Europe’s largest-ever logistics Series A ($35M) led by deep-tech investors Plural, and a recently closed Series B ($95M), Relay is scaling faster than 99% of venture-backed startups. We're assembling the most talent-dense team the logistics industry has ever seen

Relay’s Mission is to free commerce from friction. Today, high delivery costs act as a hidden tax on e-commerce, quietly shaping what can be sold online and limiting who can participate. We envision a world where more goods move more freely between more people, making the online shopping experience seamless and accessible to everyone.

THE TEAM
• ~160 people, around half in engineering, product and data
• 45+ advanced degrees across computer science, mathematics and operations research
• Thousands of data points captured, calculated, analysed and predicted for every single parcel we handle
• An intellectually vibrant culture of first‑principles thinking, tight feedback loops and relentless experimentation

The opportunity

We are looking for a Head of Capital to run how Relay raises equity and works with its investors: the next round and the ones after it, from the investor map to the close, next to the CEO.

Relay is a technology enabled parcel carrier - we deliver parcels from retailers to end customers but do it much more efficiently than incumbents. This efficiency has propelled us into one of the fastest growing companies in Europe - we have grown over 40x in the last 18 months. The capital Relay raises decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Raising it well, from the right investors, on terms we understand, is a job in its own right.

About the role

The capital we raise next decides how fast the network grows and what it can promise retailers. Our next round is planned for Q2/Q3 2027. It is for growth, from growth-stage investors, and it will be won on evidence. Today a raise runs through the CEO and the CFO alongside their day jobs. It works. It is however, not a system.

You will be the person who makes it one. You will not just be the person who holds and runs the Series C transaction, but also be the Head of the Office that will build the systems to raise multiple rounds of capital in the future. Between rounds you keep the map, the materials and the investors warm, so each raise starts from a record, not a blank page. Few roles let you own how a growing company raises the capital it runs on, from the inside, round after round.

Who you work with

- CEO: you report here. The CEO pitches and takes the decisions on a round.

- CFO: you work together daily. The CFO owns the budget, the forecast, internal finance and any debt. You own equity, the investors behind it, and the investor-facing model built from the CFO's numbers - never a second set.

- Co-founder and the Extended Leadership Team: the proof a round needs.

- External & Internal Counsel: terms and the close.

- Board: updates between rounds and approval on the round.

What you'll do

Running the transaction with the CEO & CFO

1. Build the investor map: which funds, which partner at each, why each fits us, in what order we go, and the warm path to each.

2. The process start to close: the timeline, outreach, a brief before every meeting and notes after, investor questions answered within a day, and diligence.

3. Put term sheets side by side and show what each costs in the round after. Draw up illustrative analysis and counsel the CEO on the right strategy.

4. Hold the story in one version, drafted with the CEO. The same claims and numbers across the deck, the model and the data room.

5. Own the investor-facing model: scenarios, unit economics and use of funds. Every number ties to one the CFO has signed.

Between rounds

1. Refresh the deck, the KPI pack and the data room every quarter.

2. Write investor and board updates. Answer existing investors' questions. Track what we promised them.

title: Counsel
description:
COUNSEL OPPORTUNITY

COUNSEL - eDiscovery & Information Governance

Redgrave LLP is seeking a Counsel with 5-10 years of experience leading eDiscovery workstreams in complex litigation and investigations. This position is fully remote, with some travel expected; an active license may be required in a state where the Firm has an office.This role partners with clients and merits counsel to deliver practical, defensible discovery strategy at the intersection of eDiscovery, information governance, and data privacy.

The Opportunity

In this role, you will take ownership of discovery-focused workstreams, draft sophisticated written work product, and help teams execute efficient, defensible solutions. You will be client-facing and will collaborate directly with merits counsel, co-counsel, experts, and internal teams.

Responsibilities

• Lead eDiscovery and information-governance workstreams in complex litigation and investigations.

• Draft and review discovery and governance work product, including legal memoranda, correspondence, protective orders, ESI agreements, motions, playbook components, and defensibility memoranda.

• Prepare outlines and talking points for client meetings, custodian interviews, meet-and-confers, and motion hearings.

• Coordinate with merits counsel, co-counsel, and experts; support expert task/matter management and preparation for oral testimony as needed.

• Provide practical legal advice to Firm teams; monitor emerging law and support training/policy development.

• Coach and mentor junior team members; contribute to cohesive, high-performing teams.

• Support thought leadership and practice development initiatives; identify opportunities to expand client relationships.

Qualifications

• Juris Doctor (J.D.) and active U.S. bar admission (additional admissions obtained as needed).

• 5-10 years of experience managing eDiscovery in complex litigation and investigations.

• Excellent legal writing and research skills; proven ability to draft complex discovery documents and memoranda.

• Strong project leadership and client-facing communication skills; comfort working directly with merits counsel and co-counsel.

• Technology-forward mindset and proficiency with Microsoft Office; ability to quickly learn and leverage litigation support tools.

• Willingness to travel as needed (including international travel depending on assignment).

Preferred

• Experience advising on information governance and/or data privacy issues in the litigation/investigation context.

• Experience developing defensibility positions or playbooks; participation in industry organizations and thought leadership.

PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

• Occasionally lifts objects weighing up to 10 pounds

• Frequently reaches and grasps with arms and hands; occasionally stoops and bends; must have manual dexterity

• Ability to closely examine and inspect materials

• Ability to identify and distinguish colors

• Ability to travel as needed

• Frequently uses a keyboard to enter or transform words or data

• Work is generally performed in a remote office environment with an occasional requirement to work in a normal office environment

BENEFITS

Redgrave LLP is committed to supporting our employees and ensuring their needs are met beyond the workplace. We offer a flexible portfolio of benefits and services, including medical, dental, and vision coverage, a 401(k) plan, additional benefits to help you prepare for retirement, free access to Employee Assistance Programs, and other programs designed to help you and your family stay healthy, feel secure, and enjoy a positive work/life balance.

title: Commercial Sales Development Representative
description:
About Delinea:
Delinea is the identity security platform that continuously controls what AI agents, humans and machines can do and for how long. It extends privileged access management from the point of access to the moment of action, using just-in-time authorization to reduce standing privilege across on-premises, multi-cloud and short-lived infrastructure, without adding friction for legitimate users. Delinea provides visibility across every identity type, scores the risk each one carries, and preserves the context behind access decisions, making them auditable and defensible. It supports both static and ephemeral access, letting teams apply Zero Standing Privilege where risk demands it without replacing existing infrastructure.

Position Summary:

The Commercial Sales Development Representative (C-SDR) at Delinea is a full-time, hybrid, position based at our Boston location (100 Summer Street). As an entry-level position, this role serves as a vital connection between our Sales and Marketing teams, focusing on generating and qualifying leads to create business opportunities. The Commercial SDR is responsible for initiating communication with potential customers, understanding their needs, and setting the stage for a successful sales process.

title: Account Manager - Performance Marketing (Remote Global)
description:
Description
Overview
We are looking for a Client Success Manager (Performance Marketing) to join our growing global team. In this role, you will own a portfolio of client accounts end-to-end: setting account strategy, guiding success plans tied to business KPIs, driving growth opportunities, and proactively managing retention and risk. Your portfolio will include paid media-driven accounts as well as SEO-focused accounts. The ideal candidate combines marketing strategy thinking with strong client communication, ties every decision to client ROI, and can lead cross-functional specialists (Paid Search, Paid Social, SEO, DSP, Creative, Analytics) toward clear priorities and outcomes.
This is a remote role open to candidates willing to work US business hours.
Responsibilities

• Own account strategy and success planning: define goals, KPIs, priorities, and quarterly roadmaps with each client.

• Lead client relationship and communication: run recurring meetings, manage stakeholders, align expectations from day one, and document next steps.

• Drive account performance management: interpret results against business metrics (ROAS, CPA, CAC vs. LTV, organic growth), identify issues and opportunities, and coordinate actions with channel owners.

• Identify and scope account growth opportunities: expansions, tests, and new initiatives tied to performance signals and client objectives.

• Manage account health, retention, renewal, and risk: flag risks early, create mitigation plans, and ensure consistent value delivery across a multi-client portfolio.

Why Join Finch

• Work globally, stay flexible: Join a fully distributed team across the US, LATAM, Europe, and APAC.

• Meaningful impact from day one: Your work directly influences client outcomes and how Finch grows.

• A culture built on curiosity, transparency, and ownership: We share context and empower people to make decisions.

• High-caliber teammates: Collaborate with specialists in Paid Search, Paid Social, SEO, DSP, Creative, Analytics, and more.

• Learning as a default: We encourage experimentation, cross-training, and growth as the company scales.

• Real work-life balance: We value high performance, not overwork.

Requirements

• 5+ years of experience as an Account Manager or Client Success Manager in a performance marketing or digital marketing agency (required).

• Acted as the primary point of contact (POC) for multiple client accounts simultaneously (required).

• Strong understanding of performance marketing fundamentals: paid advertising, attribution, KPIs, and optimization logic (required).

• Experience working with paid advertising-driven accounts across Paid Search, Paid Social, and Programmatic/DSP (required).

• Proven track record of improving client retention or growing accounts, with concrete examples (required).

• Fluent English, written and spoken, and comfortable leading strategic conversations with senior client stakeholders (required).

• Availability to work with consistent overlap with US business hours. (required)

• Contribuer à la définition et à l’intégration des exigences de sécurité dans les processus d’achats, de projets et de contractualisation.

• Accompagner le déploiement du dispositif sur des périmètres pilotes, notamment au moyen d’analyses de risques, de comités fournisseurs, de collectes d’évidences et, le cas échéant, d’audits ciblés.

• Tirer les enseignements des pilotes afin d’améliorer le modèle de gouvernance, les méthodes et l’outillage.

3. Passage à l’échelle et coordination transverse

• Préparer l’extension progressive du dispositif aux autres fournisseurs critiques, puis aux fournisseurs sensibles et aux nouveaux marchés, selon le périmètre retenu pour le dispositif.

title: Credentialing & Enrollment Coordinator
description:
MyOme ’s mission is to provide clinically actionable genetic information to patients throughout their lives. We combine clinical-grade whole genome sequencing, advanced AI methods for genome interpretation, and seamless digital tools for doctors and patients to order and access results. Our team is composed of seasoned entrepreneurs, scientists, and operators, and we're backed by top-tier investors.

Position Overview:
The Credentialing & Enrollment Coordinator owns MyOme ’s laboratory payer enrollment lifecycle, ensuring the lab is credentialed, enrolled, and set up to bill and get paid by every payer we work with. This role manages initial enrollments, revalidations, and maintenance across Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers, including the EDI claim and ERA/EFT enrollments that make electronic billing and payment possible. Working within our Revenue Cycle Management team, you will keep payer and provider data accurate in our billing system, so claims route correctly and remittances post cleanly. Your work directly protects cash flow and prevents denials as MyOme expands its payer network. The ideal candidate brings hands-on credentialing experience in a clinical laboratory or diagnostics setting, strong command of CMS-855B, PECOS, NPPES, and CAQH, and the organization to track dozens of applications and deadlines at once.
What You'll Do:

• Prepare, submit, and track laboratory enrollments and revalidations with Medicare (CMS-855B via PECOS), state Medicaid programs, Medicare Advantage, and commercial payers.

• Manage EDI claim enrollments (837) and ERA (835) and EFT enrollments with payers and clearinghouses, coordinating testing and go-live with the billing system vendor.

• Perform XiFin file maintenance, including payer, provider, NPI, and ordering-physician setup, so claims route and remittances post correctly.

• Maintain the lab’s credentialing data and documents, including NPPES, CAQH, CLIA and CAP certificates, state lab licenses, and W-9s, and track expiration and revalidation dates.

• Keep a credentialing and enrollment tracker current with application status, effective dates, payer IDs, and follow-up actions.

• Follow up with payers on pending applications and resolve enrollment-related denials, holds, and rejections with the billing team.

• Support network contracting by submitting post-contract enrollments and confirming loaded rates and effective dates.

• Report enrollment status, risks, and upcoming deadlines to RCM leadership, and flag anything that could delay billing.

• Document enrollment procedures and payer-specific requirements to build a repeatable process as the payer network grows.

What You'll Ne ed:

• Associate’s degree required

• 3-5 years of credentialing and payer enrollment experience, including at least 2 years in a clinical laboratory, genetic testing, or diagnostics setting.

• Hands-on experience enrolling labs (facility/group enrollment, not only individual providers) with Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial payers.

• Working knowledge of CMS-855B, PECOS, NPPES, CAQH, and CLIA requirements, and how enrollment status affects claim adjudication.

• Demonstrated experience completing EDI (837) and ERA/EFT (835) enrollments with payers and clearinghouses.

• XiFin experience strongly preferred, including payer and provider file maintenance.

• Exceptional organization and attention to detail, with a track record of managing many concurrent applications and deadlines.

• Clear, persistent communicator who can work payer provider-relations teams to resolution.

• Proficiency in Excel or Google Sheets for tracking and reporting.
